newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 1.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Residents of the small east Manawatu town of Apiti admitted on Thursday one of the townspeople had set fire to the houses of two "ratbags" to drive them out of town. Page 1.
Fletcher Challenge chief executive Hugh Fletcher said on Thursday he would step down late next year when he reached his 50th birthday. He said his decision was based on the need for change. Page 1.

Labour leader Helen Clark said on Thursday the Government had "no authority at all" to send Prime Minister Jim Bolger to the Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation forum later this month. Deputy Prime Minister Don McKinnon has raised the possibility of standing in for Bolger if, by that time, National is still the caretaker government but Bolger is needed in New Zealand for coalition talks. Clark said if there was still a caretaker government at the time of Apec the question was not who should attend, "but whether anyone should go". Page 2.
Labour leader Helen Clark on Thursday indicated it would be at least three weeks before her party and NZ First completed the preliminaries to forming any government. Page 2.

A special visa letting businesspeople pass more freely between Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation countries, including New Zealand, has been recommended in a new report by the Apec Business Advisory Council. Page 2.

The Cook Islands Government has denied receiving any offer from a Malaysian billionaire to take over most of its assets. The weekly Cook Island Press reported this week a suggestion from New Zealand media sources Malaysian businessman Tajudin Ramli was behind a NZ$100 million offer for nearly everything on the Government's asset sale list. Page 2.

A tax charge of $74.2 million took the gloss off Lion Nathan's bottom line on Thursday with tax-paid profit of $150.4 million - 25.7 percent lower than the previous year to August. However, the compant has plans for further expansion in China
through the likely purchase of a third brewery in the next 12 to 18 months. Page 14.
Fruit and vegetable processor Cedenco has forecast a $6.1 million loss for the year to September 30 after the transfer of its principal assets to Australia. Page 14.

The Commerce Commission has cleared Heinz-Wattie subsidiary Tip Top Ice Cream's application to acquire most of the assets of Dairy Group subsidiary New American Ice Cream. Commission chairman Alan Bollard said on Thursday the commission was
satisfied the proposed acquisition would not result in Tip Top acquiring or strengthening a dominant position in any market. Page 14.

Environmental issues dominated Fletcher Challenge's lengthy annual meeting in Auckland on Thursday. On the general performance of the company, chief executive Hugh Fletcher said a strategy had been implemented to deal with the difficult trading conditions for the pulp and paper division. Page 14.
State-owned Coal Corporation boosted pre-tax profits by about 10 per cent in the past June year, according to its annual report issued on Thursday. Page 14.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Air New Zealand is demanding to know how a parcel bomb carried from Asia by a competing airline ended up on a domestic flight before exploding in Wellington. As police sought international help to hunt down a prime suspect, questions were raised on Thursday night about the security of the Malaysian postal system and the exposure of airline passengers to potentially lethal cargoes.

Whom New Zealand should send to the high-powered Apec conference this month is expected to be decided by the three parties in the coalition talks - New Zealand First, Labour and National. New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said that a decision by the three parties "is the proper way to handle it". Apec is a consultative forum on economic issues with participants including the leaders of the United States and Japan.

Lion Nathan is poised for an assault on the Australian premium beer market to counter losses to Foster's light beers. Releasing results for the August year on Thursday, chief executive Doug Myers said the New Zealand premium beer sector could grow to 20 percent of the market by 2000. Lion boosted its annual operating earnings by 6.7 percent to $246.6 million.

The last major Horton family shareholder has sold out of the Auckland-based printer and publisher Wilson and Horton. Anne Kellaway, the sister of Michael Horton, confirmed she was no longer a shareholder in the company, which is the subject of a $11 a share takeover bid by the Dublin-based Independent Newspapers.
The need for life-saving surgery to the Glenbrook steel mill's costs is likely to have "some effect" on Coal Corporation's revenues, Coal Corp chief executive Ian Collinson said on Thursday.

The Commerce Commission has contacted Independent Newspapers and some shareholders of Sky Network Television ahead of INL's possible purchase of a substantial holding in Sky. A commission spokesman said the commssion had not decided whether INL's acquisition of Sky would breach the Commerce Act.
More than 100 redundancies are likely to be announced by the Fletcher Challenge Forests division before Christmas as a result of its taking control of Forestry Corporation.

Canadian media company Can West Global Communications has agreed to buy 48 percent of TV3 from Westpac Banking for $78.8 million. The purchases take effect from April next year and payment is due on September 2.
